poll.title: Preseason poll
poll.note: Four desks, four full ballots, twelve points for a first-place vote down to one. Nothing has been played, so this is entirely opinion and it gets counted like the college polls.

ballots.comment: I submitted the projection order and I will not be apologising for it. But understand what that order is worth: ten of these teams sit inside 8.3 points a week of each other. My slots two through ten are a coin flip wearing a suit. The only two entries I would defend under questioning are the bottom two, and I would defend those vigorously.

Kevin over Killian at the top, by the width of a hair. A 2.5 point weekly edge is not a reason to hand anyone a first-place vote, so I broke the tie on roster construction rather than the projection. Jack sits tenth on my ballot because his is the oldest roster in the league at 27.6 years, and age is the one number in this sport that only moves one direction.

Brian first. He built a team and then left it alone, which in this league counts as discipline. Chris is eleventh and he can take that up with the starting quarterback he released for free. And Killian is fifth, because I am not handing the top spot in my poll to a projection model. Projections do not play defense. Projections have never been punched in the mouth.

Jake first, Jerey second, and no I will not be explaining the methodology. Here is what I will explain. Every number in this poll comes from a projection of a game that has not happened, generated by a company that also wants you to click on a betting line. Odessa built her whole ballot on it. I built mine on spite. Come find me in December and we will compare.

stories.headline: Five of six games are over. Jake needs about thirty-two points from Rashee Rice
stories.body:
Denver at Kansas City is the only game left in week one. It is the last of sixteen, and no player from either team has scored anywhere in this league, which leaves four managers with a body still on the field: Justin has Kenneth Walker, Jake has Rashee Rice, Jack has Jaylen Waddle and Harrison Butker, and Jerey has the Denver defense.

Only one of those matchups is still a contest. Justin leads Jake 121.26 to 102.46, and Jake's entire comeback rests on Rice outscoring Walker by 18.80. If Walker hits his 13.7 projection, Rice needs roughly 32.5 against a projection of 12.8. If Walker has a quiet night, the bar drops toward the low twenties. Rice is not being asked for a miracle, he is being asked for the best game of his season while a teammate disappears.

Everywhere else the arithmetic has closed. Adam, Trevor, Brian, Jeff and Jomi have no starters left and all five trail. Trevor is 56.20 behind Jack with nothing on the field. Jeff is 45.96 behind Jerey with nothing on the field. Those are not comebacks in progress, they are results waiting to be recorded.
stories.storyline: Justin against Jake is the only live matchup into Monday night, with Jake needing roughly 32 points from Rashee Rice. Justin benched the Detroit defense for Tennessee and lost 11.00 points doing it, while leading by 18.80. Open question: whether that decision ends up being the margin.

takes.text: Thirty-two and a half from a receiver projected for 12.8 is a genuine outlier but not an absurd one. Call it the best week of a good receiver's season. I would put Jake somewhere around one chance in eight, which is far more than he deserves given how he got here.

The decision that may settle this has already happened. Justin started the Tennessee defense, who scored nothing, over Detroit, who scored 11.00. He leads by 18.80. If Rice takes this game by anything under eleven points, that single lineup call is the entire result and it was made on Sunday morning.

Jake needs the game of Rashee Rice's life on Monday night, and he is in that position because he started a Houston defense that scored minus one point. Minus one! You can lose a fantasy game by being outscored. He arranged to be outscored by his own defense.

Five games finished, seven managers with nothing left to do, and the whole week now rests on a Kansas City receiver and whether Kenneth Walker can be persuaded to do nothing at all. This is the most attention Kenneth Walker will receive all year.

stories.headline: Kevin named his team after Adam, drew him in week one, and put up the highest score in the league
stories.body:
162.36 to 108.32. #CrookedAdam did not just beat the man it is named after, it posted the best score in Sigma Pi B doing it. Kevin outscored all eleven other managers this week.

Ashton Jeanty went for 32.70 against a 16.0 projection. Christian Watson matched him exactly at 32.70 against 12.6. Jonathan Taylor added 25.10 and the Pittsburgh defense chipped in 20.00 against a 9.2 projection. Four starters beat their number by double digits.

Adam was not passive. Jalen Coker, the player his team is named after, scored 33.80 against an 11.9 projection, the second largest overperformance in the league this week. It was the best individual performance on a losing roster all week and it did not come close to mattering.
stories.storyline: Kevin beat Adam 162.36 to 108.32 in the grudge matchup, posting the highest score in the league. Adam's namesake Jalen Coker scored 33.80. Open question: whether Kevin's week 1 is repeatable or a ceiling game.

takes.text: On Thursday Kevin had a zero and I wrote that he had failed to show up to his own grudge. He has responded by producing the highest score in the league against the specific man he named the team after. I withdraw nothing. I simply enjoy it more now.

Adam got 33.80 from Jalen Coker. Thirty-three! The joke pick, the punchline, the man the team is named after, and he delivered the game of his life. And Adam lost by fifty-four points. That is not a bad week, that is a statement about the rest of the roster.

Worth noting that Kevin had four starters beat projection by double digits in the same week. That is a ceiling game, not a baseline. He projects second in the league at 125.5 and he scored 37 points above it. Nobody should expect this again.

I said on Thursday that Adam's lead contained no information about either roster. That was correct, and it was also the easiest call I will make all year. The honest number here is that Kevin beat his own projection by 29 percent, which is not a skill, it is a Sunday.

stories.headline: Killian scored 157.82 four days after this desk buried him twice
stories.body:
Team Ketchup put up the second highest score in the league and beat Brian 157.82 to 128.70. Jalen Hurts 30.72, Bijan Robinson 31.30, David Montgomery 28.90, Chris Olave 28.20. Four starters over 28 points.

The sequence is worth restating. Killian entered the season projected first. By Thursday he had fallen to tenth and 34 percent playoff odds, and all four desks wrote about the collapse. On Friday it emerged that the collapse was largely a missing projection for Brock Bowers being counted as a zero, and we wrote about that too. At no point in any of it had he played a down of football.

He has now played one, and he scored more than ten of the eleven other managers.
stories.storyline: Killian scored 157.82, second in the league, after being written about twice as a collapsing team. Open question: whether the preseason projection that had him first was right all along.

takes.text: I will say the thing I have been saying in a different order. We wrote about a ranking, then we wrote about the ranking being broken, and the football has now told us more in one Sunday than four days of projections managed. Killian was probably always fine.

I called him a spreadsheet's mistake and he went out and dropped 157.82. Do I regret it? No. He still has not earned anything. But I will say this much: that is what the best team in the league is supposed to look like, and it took him until Sunday to look like it.

His projection said 120.2 and he scored 157.82, so this tells us less than it appears to. What it does confirm is that the Thursday number was garbage, because a roster that produces four starters over 28 points was never the tenth best team in this league.
The invisible trophy has been taken away, given back, taken away again and has now been won on the field. I have lost track of who holds it. Killian does. For real this time. Allegedly.

stories.headline: Chris benched Isaiah Likely for 27.80 points and beat the best team in the league anyway
stories.body:
I'sah Likely to win Deebo is named after two players. Deebo Samuel started and scored 18.00. Isaiah Likely sat on the bench and scored 27.80, while Colston Loveland started at tight end and scored nothing at all.

Chris won regardless, 155.16 to 140.20, against Jomi, who holds the best projected roster in the league. Caleb Williams was the reason: 41.26 points against an 18.3 projection, the largest single performance in Sigma Pi B this week. Justin Jefferson added 31.20 and Javonte Williams 24.20.

Jomi scored 140.20, the fourth highest total in the league, and lost. He is one of two managers to score in the top half and lose, alongside Brian. Meanwhile Justin and Jerey both scored in the bottom half and won.
stories.storyline: Chris left 27.80 points from his own namesake on the bench and still beat the league's top projected roster. Jomi scored fourth in the league and lost. Open question: whether the schedule keeps punishing the teams scoring well.

takes.text: The team is called I'sah Likely to win Deebo. He benched I'sah Likely. He started a man who scored zero instead. And he beat the best roster in the league by fifteen points. There is no lesson here and I refuse to pretend otherwise.

Chris left 27.80 on the bench at a position where his starter scored nothing, and won by 14.96. That is the entire margin twice over. He is two points of Caleb Williams away from this being the worst lineup decision of the week instead of a footnote.

Jomi scored the fourth most points in this league and he is 0-1. Brian scored the sixth most and he is 0-1. Meanwhile Justin scored seventh and Jerey scored eighth and both of them are 1-0. Do not talk to me about who is good. Talk to me about who the schedule likes.

This is the argument for the all-play record, which the site will start showing once the week closes. Jomi beat eight of the eleven other managers on Sunday and has nothing to show for it. Over a full season those gaps close. Over one week they decide everything.

stories.headline: The bench ledger: 117 points that nobody started
stories.body:
Six managers left double figures on the bench at a position where their starter underperformed. Chris was the worst offender at 27.80 and got away with it. Trevor was second and did not: he benched Dallas Goedert for 23.70 and started Kyle Pitts, who scored nothing, in a game he lost by 56.20.

Jeff is the one to sit with. He has made exactly one transaction this season, adding Devaughn Vele. Vele scored 19.90 on Sunday. Jeff started Drake London, who scored 5.50, and lost 118.70 to 72.74. He made one good decision all year and then declined to act on it.

Adam benched Kyle Monangai for 20.40 while starting Kenny Gainwell for 2.80. Jerey benched T.J. Hockenson for 13.60 while starting AJ Barner for 3.30. And Justin, who leads the only live game in the league by 18.80, benched the Detroit defense for 11.00 to start a Tennessee defense that scored nothing at all.
stories.storyline: Six managers left double-digit points on the bench in week 1, led by Chris at 27.80 and Trevor at 23.70. Jeff benched the only player he has added all season. Open question: whether lineup efficiency separates this league more than roster quality does.

takes.text: Jeff made one move all season. One! He went out, identified Devaughn Vele, added him, and then left him on the bench to watch Drake London score 5.50. That is not a fantasy manager. That is a man filling out a form.

Trevor is the genuinely painful one. Goedert for 23.70 instead of Pitts for nothing, in a week he lost by 56.20. It would not have changed the result, which is precisely why it will annoy him for a month.

Once this week closes the site will publish lineup efficiency, which is actual points divided by the most the roster could have produced. I expect the spread on that number to be wider than the spread on roster quality, and I expect it to explain more of this league's results than the draft ever will.
One hundred and seventeen points sat on benches in this league on Sunday. That is more than Jeff scored with his actual team. I want that framed.

stories.headline: CORRUPT COMMISSIONER BUILDS FANTASY NEWS SITE THAT ABSOLUTELY NOBODY READS
stories.body:
Let me explain the arrangement. The commissioner of this league, a man who runs a team called Coker? I hardly know her! and whose own leaguemate named a franchise #CrookedAdam out of what I can only assume is documented grievance, decided that Sigma Pi B required a newsroom. He did not ask whether anyone wanted one. He built it, he staffed it, and he pays it in exposure.

So we got to work. We built a draft report card that values every player against the last startable body at his own position. We run five thousand simulations of the remaining season every time somebody loads the page. We calculate what your record would be under all eleven other schedules. We caught a missing projection for a tight end that had silently deleted a starter from a roster and made a good team look like the tenth best in the league. We publish the losing waiver bids. We keep a record book going back three seasons. There is a betting board now. There is a poll with four full ballots that get graded against reality so nobody can quietly pretend they said something else.

And the readership? Twelve men. Twelve. Nine of whom left double figures on the bench this week. One of whom made a single transaction all season, correctly identified Devaughn Vele, added him, and then started somebody else. A starting NFL quarterback sat unclaimed on the waiver wire for a full week while this desk screamed about it into a void with a dark green background. I have checked the analytics. There are no analytics. The commissioner did not build any. Of course he didn't.
stories.storyline: The newsroom exists because the commissioner decided it should, and has no evidence anyone reads it. Open question: whether a single manager changes a lineup because of something published here.

takes.text: I want to gently distance the rest of the desk from that column. It is unedited, it names the commissioner, and the claim about analytics is unverifiable because, as stated, there are no analytics. That said, I have also not been paid, and I would like that noted somewhere.

FINALLY somebody says it. I have been screaming about Jeff's bench for a week! A WEEK! Devaughn Vele scored 19.90 sitting down! And not one man in this league has messaged me about it. Not one. You people do not deserve a newspaper. You deserve a group chat and a spreadsheet and I hope you are very happy together.

For the record, the readership figure of twelve is an assumption, not a measurement. The true number is unknown and could plausibly be lower. I would also note that if every manager read every word we published and acted on none of it, the observable data would look exactly as it does now. We cannot distinguish being ignored from being ineffective.

The commissioner built an entire media operation, hired four people, gave us real numbers and full editorial freedom, and then went out and lost by fifty-four points to a team named after how much everyone distrusts him. I would not change a thing. This is the best job I have ever had and I am not employed.
